<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This file is a `.SRCINFO` metadata file for the AUR package `dropwatch-music`. It contains standard packaging information: package description, version, dependencies, architecture, license, and source URL with a verified SHA-256 checksum. The source is fetched from the project's own GitHub repository (`https://github.com/carnager/dropwatch/archive/v0.1.5.tar.gz`), and the checksum is provided (not `SKIP`), which is the ordinary practice for verifying source integrity. The dependencies (`glibc`, `tar`, `xz`, and `go` as makedependency) are standard for a Go-based AUR package. There are no suspicious network requests, obfuscated code, dangerous commands (`eval`, `base64`, `curl`, `wget` in unexpected contexts), or unexpected file operations. The package description ("Shows which albums by the artists in your music library you are missing") is consistent with the application's stated purpose. No injected malicious code or supply-chain attack indicators are present in this metadata file.
</details>

<details>
The PKGBUILD is a standard AUR package definition for dropwatch-music. It references the official dropwatch GitHub repository via a properly formatted tarball URL, includes a valid SHA256 checksum, and follows conventional build and installation procedures using Go. There are no signs of supply chain compromise: the source is from the project's own upstream, the checksum is explicitly provided (not SKIP), and all operations are confined to installing the application's own binaries and configuration files within the package directory. The build process uses standard Go tooling (go mod download, go build) without executing external scripts or making unexpected system modifications. No obfuscation, data exfiltration, or backdoor indicators are present.
</details>
